# **PRECIOUS METALS QUARTERLY INDUSTRY AND MARKET OUTLOOK** **Independent analysis of the gold, platinum, palladium and silver markets** www.cruanalysis.com ## **AN ESSENTIAL RESOURCE FOR THE GLOBAL PRECIOUS METALS INDUSTRY** The best market analysis and clearly argued forecasts are essential in today’s decision-making environment. CRU’s Precious Metals Market Outlook provides authoritative insights into the latest market trends and developments and presents you with five-year forecasts of supply, demand and prices. #### **Comprehensive coverage** Issuing written reports four times a year, the Precious Metals Service provides you with quarterly forecasts for the next two years and annual forecasts for a further three years. This is achieved by analysis of key market dynamics such as fabrication demand, mine production, investor trends, producer hedging, central bank activities, and various external influences, such as trade flows, inflation, interest and exchange rates. - Critical, objective and authoritative analysis - Constant market analysis and a wealth of data available via internet access - Monthly market analysis and 1-year forecasts via e-mail and written report - Quarterly market analysis and 5-year forecasts via e-mail and written report - Understanding the trends and changes in physical and investment demand - Providing data on the mining industry – production and hedging - Mobilisation of central bank and private sector gold stocks - Influence of external factors such as exchange, interest and inflation rates #### **Extranet access service** CRU’s password protected Extranet offers you unlimited access to downloadable files of the reports and the statistical data contained in the chapters and appendices. The data is updated every quarter. As each new edition is posted to the site, previous editions are archived, building into your own historical database. **2** PRECIOUS METALS QUARTERLY INDUSTRY AND MARKET OUTLOOK Precious Metals Quarterly 1Q2007 Platinum 31
Forecast update: strength in autocatalyst sector to offset weaker jewellery demand Since the platinum price spiked at an all-time record high of $1,355/oz in nominal terms last November, platinum has made steady gains from the low $1,100’s/oz to trade around the $1,250s at the end of 2007 Q1 - with just one correction that temporarily set the market back. This quarter we take a look at some of the developments in the two major offtake sectors for platinum that could impact demand over the next couple of years. **Autocatalysts** #### **The industry benchmark** Independent and authoritative – CRU is the largest and longest established consultancy specialising in the metals and mining industries. at elevated levels over the forecast period, and combined with ongoing concerns over the

Continued strong growth in Asian vehicle manufacturing will very likely offset weakness in the European and North American markets. Adding to this is the introduction of new legislation for light, medium and heavy-duty diesel vehicles in Japan in 2009, which (as in Europe) target specifically NOx and PM emissions (see Table 8) and the possible implementation of a new policy in Seoul. As part of plans to improve air quality in the city, the Seoul Metropolitan Government is aiming to ensure that all older diesel-powered trucks (those over seven years old) that weigh over 3.5t are fitted with diesel particulate filters by the end of 2008. Drivers who fail to comply could incur penalty charges. In the light truck sector, Korea manufactured more than 220,000 units in 2006 and this figure could rise by 46% over the net four years. **Jewellery** Jewellery is the one component of demand that has really been pressurised by the high and volatile prices, with consumers at the more price-sensitive fashion end turning to white gold and palladium. Even in Europe, one of the most price-inelastic regions for platinum jewellery offtake (having remained between 190-195koz from 2003 to 2005, during which time the platinum price increased by 30%), demand contracted by some 20koz in 2006. CRU expects jewellery demand to remain weak in 2007 on the back of further price appreciation, and we could even see offtake in China, which accounts for about 45% of global platinum jewellery demand, fall by a similar percentage this year as in 2006. This will, in part, depend on the extent to which manufacturers and retailers take advantage of any price dips to restock inventories following recycling activities. However, a plan to raise consumption tax on Precious Metals Quarterly 1Q2007 Platinum 33 luxury goods in C

hina, including jewellery, could offset on new purchases of the metal for restocking purposes. On the other side of the coin, platinum’s high price really enforces its image as a luxury metal and for this reason offtake in the bridal or high-end sector is expected to remain fairly buoyant in most markets (providing we do not see price spikes of the magnitude experienced in November 2006). Not all regions are immune though - reports indicate that substitution occurred in the USA bridal sector in 2006, and we see no reason for this not to continue this year. Demand for platinum jewellery in India grew by 30% in 2006, with offtake notably
improving (competing with gold) during the Indian wedding season, which began in mid-
January. Both traditional and modern jewellers saw significant growth in demand for the metal
during the festive season – previously considered an auspicious gold buying occasion. Platinum
jewellery was introduced into this country at prices of more than $1,200/oz. The Platinum

For our estimate of the final balance in the platinum market in 2006, we previously forecast that
the market would be in marginal surplus by about 17,000oz. However, recently released trade
data for the full year 2006 shows that Russian annual derived shipments from stock were far
lower than expected. Notably imports into Switzerland, Japan, the USA, China and Hong Kong
were all lower (in some cases much lower) compared with previous years. Shipments from
stock were only slightly more than half that recorded in 2005, yet total Russian production was
likely only down by about 20koz. Therefore, while the basic balance for 2006 (excluding stock
movements) shows the market wa

s in surplus by about 90koz, the final balance comes in at a
deficit of about 330koz.

**4** PRECIOUS METALS QUARTERLY INDUSTRY AND MARKET OUTLOOK 



#### **Typical contents** 

The written report contains an executive summary giving you a quick overview of the outlook for all the precious metals. The main body of the report contains analysis and discussion in separate chapters dedicated to gold, platinum, palladium and silver. All chapters are emailed to subscribers several days before dispatch of the printed version. A wealth of statistical data on prices, stocks, mine output, consumption and trade supports the analysis and is presented in the form of Excel Spreadsheets. This data is available to subscribers via CRU's extranet where the statistical data is updated regularly. 

The Precious Metals Quarterly service is supported by CRU's acclaimed monthly Precious Metals Monitor. This monthly publication provides analysis of the latest developments in the gold, silver, platinum and palladium markets and presents CRU's view of how these metal markets may develop in the short term. Regular features include developments in prices, mine production, consumption, imports into main end-user markets, central bank activity and leading indicators for spot and futures business in gold, silver and platinum group metals.

#### **The leading business consultants in metals and mining** 

CRU is the world’s leading independent consultancy, business analysis and conferences provider focusing on the mining, metals, power, cables, fertilisers and chemicals sectors. Founded in the late 1960s and privately owned to ensure its independence, CRU is located in London, Beijing, Sydney, Rio de Janeiro, Santiago and key centres in the United States. Employing more than 200 experts comprising economists, management consultants, engineers, metallurgists, geologists, chemists and journalists, we are the world’s foremost consultancy in the metals industry.
